newsitem.title: MOROCCO: King Hassan says door open for talks with Polisario.
newsitem.headline: King Hassan says door open for talks with Polisario.

text.p: King Hassan of Morocco said on Wednesday the door "remains open" for talks with the independence-seeking Polisario Front in the disputed Western Sahara.

Speaking on the 21st anniversary of the "Green March" by 350,000 Moroccans into the territory then under Spanish control, the king said talks had been held recently in Morocco with the Polisario but had collapsed.

"We agreed to meet them but on condition that the question of independence was not on the table. Our son (Crown Prince Sidi Mohammed) and the Interior Minister (Driss Basri) held talks with them during two days," the king said.
King Hassan, in a live broadcast, said it was expected that he would meet Polisario representatives personally if the initial talks brought results.
"But they still don't understand that the (Western) Sahara became Moroccan and even if we want to give the territory another aspect or legal definition, we cannot," he said.
"The talks ended (but) not on the basis of a breakdown. We agreed to leave the door open when matters have matured."
Polisario, seeking independence for the former Spanish colony, has been locked in conflict with Morocco, which claims the territory, for more than two decades.
In September, the two sides met in Rabat for their first direct talks since 1989 when delegations met in Marrakesh in Morocco. Late last month, Morocco freed 66 Polisario prisoners.

A ceasefire ended hostilities in the territory in September 1991 and a U.N.-sponsored referendum was due to be held the following January. It has been delayed in endless wrangles as to who, among the nomadic Saharans, are eligible to vote.
King Hassan, in his speech, told Polisario "if you have something new, please come quickly for talks, within the framework of the U.N. peace plan. Morocco is committed to it."
